english.html: upheld all his acts <sup class="mk" data-key="k">k</sup>, although the Emperor Augustus commanded that such kinds of slaves, so rash as to thrust themselves by like substitutions into dignities, be punished with fitting penalties <sup class="mk" data-key="l">l</sup>. The Pontiff Clement III, speaking of a seditious priest who, after having falsely usurped the name and title of a King's son, and stirred up the people to civil wars, was condemned first to the whip, and afterwards to be hanged on a gibbet, where he was executed, calls into doubt whether those who put him to death are excommunicated <sup class="mk" data-key="m">m</sup>. Of which I should not have doubted, if the substitution alone had deserved death. One reads further that Trebellius Calca substituted upon himself the name and person of the son of Clodius, to ravish and take possession of his goods, and that the fraud could not be so finely covered but that in the end the light of truth brought it to evidence, whereby he lost his cause: but that he was punished for such fraud and substitution, history says nothing of it <sup class="mk" data-key="n">n</sup>. So of the Milanese woman who called herself Rubria, in order to occupy and invade the goods of the true Rubria, deceased: one reads indeed that she succumbed through the prudence of Octavian Augustus; but that she was punished, there is no author who speaks of it <sup class="mk" data-key="o">o</sup>. I am not ignorant either that others have been punished for such substitutions, doubtful enough however. Herophilus, a physician, who called himself the son of the younger Marius, acquired so much favour and grace with the people, for the memory of Caius Marius, his pretended grandfather, who had been seven times consul at Rome, that several companies of the old soldiers, and of the towns, followed him as their ancient patron and protector: nay, when Caesar had returned victorious from Spain against the children of Pompey, those who came to congratulate him on his victory did no less honour to Herophilus than to Caesar, whose trophies and monuments were nevertheless already engraved in every corner of the earth: whereat Caesar, indignant, and fearing some sedition of the people, only banished him from Rome. True it is that after the death of Caesar, because he returned to Rome and threatened the Senate, he was by command of the Senators made prisoner, and in the house [the prison, in Valerius Maximus] executed to death <sup class="mk" data-key="p">p</sup>. ſerfs ſi temeraires de ſingerer par ſemblables ſuppoſi-
tions aux dignite, l'Empereur Auguſte ait commandé
les punir de peines conuenables {l}. Le Pontife Clement
iij. parlant d'vn preſtre ſeditieux, lequel apres auoir fau
ſement vſurpé le nom & titre de fils de Roy, & eſmeu
le peuple à guerres ciuiles, fut condamné premiere-
ment au fouët, & apres eſtre pendu à vn gibet, où fut
executé, reuoque en doute, ſi ceux qui l'ont fait mourir,
ſont excommuniez {m}. Dequoy n'euſſe douté, ſi la ſeule
ſuppoſition euſt merité la mort. On lit bien d'auanta-
ge, que Trebellius Calca ſuppoſa le nom & la per-
ſonne du fils de Clodius, pour rauir & ſ'emparer de ſes
biens, & que la fraude ne ſceut eſtre ſi finement couuer
te, qu'en fin la lumiere de la verité nè la miſt en euiden
ce, dont il perdit ſa cauſe: mais qu'il fuſt puni de telle
fraude, & ſuppoſition, l'hiſtoire n'en parle point {n}. Ain-
ſi de la femme Milanoiſe, qui ſe diſoit Rubrie, pour
occuper & enuahir les biens de la vraye Rubrie defun-
cte. On lit bien qu'elle ſuccõba par la prudence d'Octa
uian Auguſte: mais qu'elle fut punie, n'y a aucũ autheur
qui en parole {o}. Ie n'ignore pas auſſi que d'autres n'ayẽt
eſté punis pour telles ſuppoſitions, aſſez douteuſes
toutesfois. Herophile medecin, qui ſe diſoit fils du ieu
ne Marius acquiſt tant de faueur & grace enuers le peu
ple, pour la memoire de Caius Marius, ſon ayeul pretẽ-
du, qui auoit eſté ſept fois conſul a Rome, que pluſi-
eurs compagnies des vieux ſoldats, & des villes, le ſuy-
uoyent comme leur ancien patron & protecteur: voi-
re quand Ceſar fut retourné d'Eſpagne victorieux,
contre les enfans de Pompée, ceux qui le venoyent
feliciter de ſa victoire, ne faiſoyent pas moins d'hon-
neur à Herophile qu'à Ceſar, duquel pourtant les tro-
phées & monumens eſtoyent ia grauez par tous les
anglets de la terre: dont Ceſar indigné, & craignant
quelque ſedition de peuple, le bannit ſeulement de
Rome: vray eſt qu'apres la mort de Ceſar; partant qu'il
retourna à Rome, & menaçoit le Senat, il fut par le
commandement des Senateurs fait priſonnier, &
dans la maiſon executé à mort {p}. En outre, nous li-
